Class bayesnecjointfit of one model fitted across the levels of a factor

Source: R/bayesnecjointfit-class.R
bayesnecjointfit-class.Rd

Returned by bnec_joint applied to a bayesnecgroupfit. Each level is fitted the equation its own weights favour, with every curve parameter taking a separate value per level of the grouping factor within a single posterior.

Details

The object holds the fit and the level structure and nothing derived from a prediction grid. A level term is a population-level term, so re_formula = NA does not drop it and the prediction grid has to name a level: bnec_newdata on a joint refit returns resolution rows for each level rather than resolution rows, with the level varying slowest.

ecx, nsec, nec and ecnsec therefore return a data.frame with one row per level, named in a level column, rather than the named vector of three they return for a bayesnecfit. For ecx and nsec that is the same table a bayesnecgroupfit returns, so the two routes can be read against each other. ecnsec has no bayesnecgroupfit method. On a joint refit it returns, at each level, the percent effect at the nsec supplied, which is one value for every level, read off that level's own curve as ecnsec reads it off a single fit. Its columns are named as those of the ecx table — Q50, Q2.5 and Q97.5 under the default prob_vals — where ecnsec on a single fit keeps the names quantile gives. Its bound_ columns are empty, because ecnsec records no censoring. exceedance returns one row per level, preceded by a level column, as it does for a bayesnecgroupfit. autoplot() draws one panel per level and ggbnec_data names the level in a panel column, again matching the grouped fit.

nec adds two columns, because a composed refit fits one equation per level and only some equations estimate a nec parameter: model names the equation fitted at that level and ne_type the type of the estimate reported there. By default the estimate is the nec parameter, which is NA at a level whose equation has none; nec(x, no_effect = TRUE) reports instead the NSEC of that level's own fitted curve there, and labels the row "NSEC". One equation per level is what makes that label possible: the model-averaged estimate of a bayesmanecfit mixes NEC and NSEC draws in proportion to the model weights and so has no single type to report.

Each level is estimated on its own grid, one level at a time, rather than from one prediction spanning them all. A control posterior, an ECx crossing and an NSEC search each read a single monotone curve, and a grid holding every level concatenated is not one: the crossing search would find the first level's crossing and report it for the fit.

The coefficient one level holds on one parameter is named b_<parameter>_<group_var><level> in the draws — b_top_sitea for level "a" of a grouping variable named site — where every level was fitted the same equation. The level part is the label as brms renames it, which drops a space and spells out some punctuation, so level "Site A" is b_top_siteSiteA. Where the levels were fitted different equations, each level's parameters are brms non-linear parameters in their own right and the name is b_<parameter><level tag>_Intercept, the tag being the level name reduced to letters and digits followed by Lv and its rank in the sorted level set. print() reports the tags.

See methods(class = "bayesnecjointfit") for an overview of available methods.

Slots

fit

The brmsfit.

model

The equation fitted at every level, or NA where the levels favoured different equations.

models

A named character vector, the equation fitted at each level.

level_spec

The level structure the fit was built from: the level tags, indicator columns and mask values where the equations differ, and the grouping variable and levels either way.

level_weights

The weight the equation fitted at each level holds at that level, from the grouped fit. A level's own weights sum to one, so this is the share of that level's evidence behind the equation used there.

bayesnecformula

The bayesnecformula the fit was built from, carrying the equation of the first level.

init

The initial values the fit was given.

group_var

The name of the grouping column.

levels

The factor levels, in the order their coefficients are in.

disp_by_level

Whether the family's dispersion parameter was also given a value per level.

data

The data.frame fitted, all levels.

family

The family, carried over from the grouped fit.

model_weights

The summed model weight of every equation across the levels of the grouped fit, in decreasing order.

model_weight_share

The share of the summed weight the forced equation holds, between 0 and 1, where model named one. NA where each level was fitted its own equation, because no equation was imposed on the set for such a share to describe, and NA where model named an equation no level fitted.
